title: Stability Translation Workbench — initiative log and action ticker
body:
Purpose: capture rapid decisions, mapping rules, and the execution ticker for the 'translation workbench' — the small program to convert product-level service promises into measurable SLO objects, test harnesses, and rollout criteria. This doc is the canonical working log for cross-team conversation between Product, Platform, Serving Runtime, and Observability.

Summary of approach: we treat 'translation' as a two-step pipeline: 1) interpret product commitment (what customers feel) into candidate SLOs and guardrails; 2) validate candidate SLOs via lightweight probes and a canary window before formal adoption. The workbench will store mappings (service -> metric -> threshold -> remediation), confidence score, and an action ticker for outstanding decisions.

Goals (30/60/90 lens):
- 30d: shipping a minimal translation template; pilot with 2 feature teams (chat-generation and embeddings route). Basic automation to generate candidate SLO drafts from metric sets and traffic patterns.
- 60d: integrate probes into the existing observability pipelines; add rollout safety checks (traffic split, fallback model mapping). Run two live canaries and capture false positives/negatives.
- 90d: formalize handoff process: owner signoff checklist, runbook snippet, and a small web UI to view translations and decision history.

Success metrics (how we know the initiative works):
- Time to first SLO draft after product ask < 3 business days.
- False positive alert rate from translation probes < 5% in pilot teams.
- 2 successful feature rollouts using translation outputs within 90 days.

Key stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Product: articulate the customer-facing promise and uptime/latency expectations.
- Observability: implement probes, provide metric families and dashboards.
- Serving Runtime: advise on feasible thresholds considering batching/KV cache behavior.
- Platform (SRE): own the final SLO object, alerting, and runbook entry.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: map customer SLAs to SLO change requests.

Milestones & decisions (action ticker):
- 2026-09-16: Confirm metric families for chat-generation (latency p50/p99, token-error-rate, model-fallback-rate). ACTION: Observability to publish metric list. Owner: Olivia. STATUS: done.
- 2026-09-20: Decide canonical confidence scale for translation (low/medium/high). ACTION: Cross-team vote. Owner: Nora. STATUS: done. Rationale: use simple 3-pt scale to avoid paralysis.
- 2026-09-24: Probe window length for p99 latency (initial: 30m rolling). ACTION: Observability to test sensitivity. Owner: Ethan. STATUS: in_progress.
- 2026-09-30: Decide fallback SLO policy when cache-thrashing spikes observed. ACTION: Platform to propose automatic fallback mapping. Owner: Samir. STATUS: open.

Runbook & rollout safety notes:
- Canary criteria (must pass all three): metrics within candidate thresholds for 2x window length; no more than 1 emergency rollback trigger in window; fallback path exercised in sim.
- Escalation path: on canary breach -> auto-traffic shift to safe variant (0.0XX). Pager: on-call SRE -> week rotation owner -> product manager.
- Soft rollback: lower concurrency or increase batching window before model downgrade to avoid quality regressions.

Risks & mitigations (rapid list):
- Risk: thresholds too tight cause noisy alerts. Mitigation: use confidence=low for first 14 days and suppress automated alerting, only log and surface to dashboard.
- Risk: metric ambiguity across teams (same name, different unit). Mitigation: enforce metric families and examples in template; include metric unit column.
- Risk: translation encourages brittle SLOs tied to transient infra constraints. Mitigation: add 'feasibility note' from Serving Runtime prior to SLO adoption.

Open questions (to resolve in the next sync):
- How to represent user-perceived quality (semantic correctness) as an SLO? Current plan: store evaluator-set refs and link to Redwood Optimize eval run ids.
- What level of automation for mapping product request -> SLO should exist before requiring human signoff? Proposal: automation drafts + human signoff always required for first 2 adoptions per team.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Observability: run sensitivity experiments for p99 probe window (Ethan) due 2026-09-22. DONE.
- Platform: draft fallback mapping options (Samir) due 2026-09-26. IN_PROGRESS.
- Product: provide 3 customer promise examples for embeddings route (Priya) due 2026-09-20. DONE.

Artifacts to link when drafting final SLO objects: Confluence (translation template), JIRA tickets for rollout, GH PR for infra changes, eval run ids.

Meeting rhythm and collaboration pattern:
- Twice-weekly 30m sync for the pilot weeks (Mon/Wed). Async decision log updated after each sync.
- Biweekly demo when pilot hits 60d to show canary results to exec stakeholders.

Notes-to-self / scratch:
- keep the translation template short; one page with examples and one checklist. Avoid heavy gates.
- consider 'confidence decay' when traffic mix changes (re-run translation after 10%+ shift in model roster or region routing).

Appendix (links & quick examples):
- Example translation snippet: product promise = "responses under 300ms for interactive chat 95% of time" -> candidate SLO: latency p95 < 300ms measured on user-facing edge proxy; measurement window 24h; confidence low-medium; probe endpoint = /edge/latency-v1.
- Example runbook excerpt: on p95 breaches -> verify model variant mapping -> check recent deploys -> escalate if deploy less than 30m old.

If you're editing this doc: append a short note with date and your initials at the bottom of the file. Keep the action ticker current — it should be the single source of truth for outstanding translation decisions.
